title: King and rook against king: cut off and close in
outcomes: Uses the rook to cut the lone king off along a file
Brings the king up close, then finishes with a rook check on the edge
Knows a check next to the king fails if the rook is unprotected

steps.text: A rook alone cannot mate: the lone king can chase it. So cut the king off with the rook along a file or a rank, then bring your own king up close, so that it covers the squares the black king would run to. The rook then gives the final check on the edge.

steps.caption: The rook on d1 holds the whole d-file. The black king cannot cross it.

steps.title: Two ways to use the rook
steps.prompt: In this position White can also check at once with the rook, Rg8+. Predict first: does that work as well as bringing the king, Ke6?
Did you manage the king-and-rook ending without stalemate and without losing the rook? How sure are you of the method now? (low / medium / high)
